info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package captable is your cap table: stakeholders, share classes, grants, SAFEs, rounds, and who owns what.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's share classes, in creation order.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's share classes, in creation order. A
share class is what a certificate is issued in, and every class the company
has authorized appears. The response is a bare JSON array, not an envelope.

post.summary: Defines a new class of shares.
post.description:
Defines a new class of shares.

Every field but convertsToShareClassId is required — a class is the instrument
every later issuance prices against, so a partially-specified one would silently
mis-value every share issued into it. `seniority` orders liquidation preference
with LOWER first.

patch.description:
Replaces one share class's terms.

It is a full REPLACE and not a merge, despite the PATCH: every field is written
as sent, so a field omitted is written empty rather than left alone. Send the
whole class. The method is PATCH because the resource is addressed by id, not
because the body is partial — and getting that backwards silently blanks terms
every later issuance prices against.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID addresses the resource. The URL is the addressing authority — a path
segment binds after the body and after the query — so the address decides
which row is written whatever a body claims.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's cap-table company record.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's cap-table company record. The row is
seeded when the tenant's store first opens, so it always exists; its name and
incorporation details are set with PUT /v1/captable/company.

put.summary: Sets the caller org's company name and incorporation details.
put.description:
Sets the caller org's company name and incorporation details.
The name is required; the three incorporation fields are optional and each is
stored as empty when omitted, so a call that sends only a name CLEARS them.
The company row itself is seeded when the tenant's store first opens, so this
never creates one.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's convertible notes, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's convertible notes, newest first. A
note's principal sits OUTSIDE issued equity until it converts, so it is not
part of the share counts.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's convertible notes, taking its principal out of the cap table's unconverted-instrument totals.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's convertible notes, taking its
principal out of the cap table's unconverted-instrument totals. An id this org
does not hold is not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the convertible note to delete.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's investments, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's investments, newest first. It spans
every round, so it is the flat ledger of cheques written into the company,
each naming its investor and the round it went into.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's option grants, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's option grants, newest first. Each row is
joined to its grantee and its equity plan. Grants that are EXERCISED, EXPIRED
or CANCELLED are listed here but do not dilute the cap table.

post.summary: Grants options to a stakeholder from an equity plan.
post.description: Grants options to a stakeholder from an equity plan.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's option grants, taking its shares out of the cap table's granted-options and fully-diluted counts.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's option grants, taking its shares
out of the cap table's granted-options and fully-diluted counts. An id this org
does not hold is not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the option grant to delete.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's equity plans, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's equity plans, newest first. An equity
plan is an option pool: a reserve of shares, drawn from one share class, that
option grants are written against.

post.summary: Opens an equity plan that options are granted from.
post.description: Opens an equity plan that options are granted from.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's fundraising rounds, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's fundraising rounds, newest first. A round
groups a fundraising event; a PRICED round also carries the share class and
price per share it issues at.

post.summary: Opens a priced round that investments can be added to.
post.description:
Opens a priced round that investments can be added to.

The round opens OPEN; investing into a closed one is refused.

get.summary: Returns one of the caller org's fundraising rounds together with every investment written into it, oldest first.
get.description:
Returns one of the caller org's fundraising rounds together with every
investment written into it, oldest first. A round id that does not exist in the
caller's org is not found — including one that exists in another tenant, since
the org comes from the caller's principal and is part of the lookup.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the round to read. It is the path segment: the URL is the addressing
authority, and the org it is resolved in comes from the caller's principal,
so an id from another tenant is simply not found.

post.summary: Closes one of the caller org's fundraising rounds, recording the close date and moving its status to CLOSED.
post.description:
Closes one of the caller org's fundraising rounds, recording the
close date and moving its status to CLOSED. Only an OPEN round can be closed:
a round that is already closed — like an id this org does not hold — is not
found. Closing a round does not change what was invested in it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the round to close. It is the path segment: the URL is the
addressing authority, and the org it is resolved in comes from the
caller's principal, so an id from another tenant is simply not found.

post.summary: Records one investor's money into an open round.
post.description:
Records one investor's money into an open round.

The round must be OPEN; investing into a closed one is refused. Where the round
carries a price per share, the investment also issues the shares it buys and the
answer names them.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the round to invest in. The URL is the addressing authority — a path
segment binds after the body and after the query — so the address decides
which round is written whatever a body claims.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's SAFEs, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's SAFEs, newest first. A SAFE is a simple
agreement for future equity: its capital sits OUTSIDE issued equity until it
converts, so it is not part of the share counts.

post.summary: Records a SAFE — a simple agreement for future equity.
post.description: Records a SAFE — a simple agreement for future equity.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's SAFEs, taking its capital out of the cap table's unconverted-instrument totals.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's SAFEs, taking its capital out of the
cap table's unconverted-instrument totals. An id this org does not hold is not
found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the SAFE to delete.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's share certificates, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's share certificates, newest first. Each row
is joined to its holder and its share class, so a certificate names who holds
it and what class it is in without a second call.

post.summary: Issues a share certificate to a stakeholder.
post.description:
Issues a share certificate to a stakeholder.

The certificate id must be UNIQUE within the company — a duplicate is refused
409, not silently merged — and both the stakeholder and the share class must
belong to this company, so an id from another tenant is a 400 rather than a
cross-company issuance.

post.summary: Moves shares from one stakeholder to another.
post.description:
Moves shares from one stakeholder to another.

Omit `quantity` to transfer the whole certificate, which REASSIGNS it and mints
no new share. Send a quantity below the amount held to SPLIT it — the source
certificate keeps the remainder, and a split additionally requires
`certificateId` for the new certificate, which must be unique in the company.
A quantity outside 1..held is refused, so a transfer can never over-issue.

Both outcomes answer 200: a transfer records a movement between holders and
mints no security of its own, which is why this is not a 201 the way an
investment is.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's share certificates, taking its shares out of the cap table's outstanding and fully-diluted counts.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's share certificates, taking its
shares out of the cap table's outstanding and fully-diluted counts. An id this
org does not hold is not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the share certificate to delete.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's stakeholders, newest first.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's stakeholders, newest first. The
response is a bare JSON array, not an envelope. Each row carries the holder's
contact and address fields alongside the company's name.

post.summary: Add stakeholders to the cap table
post.description:
Records the people and institutions that can hold equity — the rows every share, option, SAFE, note and investment is issued to.

The body is ONE stakeholder object or an ARRAY of them, and the array is the point: a whole roster loads in a single call. Email is the identity within the company, so a stakeholder whose email is already on the table is SKIPPED rather than duplicated or rejected — the 201 reports how many rows were actually inserted, which is what makes re-running an import safe. Validation is all-or-nothing across the batch: one bad entry refuses the whole array.

Writes the caller's OWN cap table: the org resolved from the validated principal selects the tenant's store and scopes every row, so there is no field by which a caller can write into another company's table; a request with no validated org is refused. The whole write runs in one transaction, so a refusal leaves nothing behind. Validation is the cap-table bundle's and so is its refusal: a bad body comes back as {success:false, message, errors:[…]} with the failing fields listed, and numeric fields accept a number OR a numeric string. Bodies are capped at 1 MiB.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's stakeholders.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's stakeholders. It REFUSES to
orphan issued equity: a holder that still holds share certificates or option
grants cannot be deleted, and answers 400 saying so — release or transfer the
holdings first. An id this org does not hold is not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the stakeholder to delete.

patch.summary: Changes one of the caller org's stakeholders.
patch.description:
Changes one of the caller org's stakeholders. It is a
PARTIAL update: only the fields the request names are written, and a field
sent as null clears that column. A request that names no updatable field is
refused, and an id this org does not hold is not found.

The values are stored as sent. Unlike adding a stakeholder, this route does
not check the email's shape or the type and relationship vocabularies, so it
can record a value that adding one would have rejected.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID is the stakeholder to update. It is the path segment: the URL is the
addressing authority, and the org it is resolved in comes from the
caller's principal, so an id from another tenant is simply not found.

get.summary: Computes the caller org's cap table.
get.description:
Computes the caller org's cap table. It answers who owns what on a
fully-diluted basis: outstanding shares, granted options, per-stakeholder
ownership percentages, each share class's authorized versus issued position,
and the capital sitting on SAFEs and convertible notes that have not yet
converted. Only non-terminal option grants dilute — EXERCISED, EXPIRED and
CANCELLED grants are excluded, so equity issued through an exercised option is
never counted twice.

issued.description: Issued is how many shares of the class have been issued.

shareClassId.description: ShareClassID addresses the class this position is for.

incorporationType.description: IncorporationType is the entity kind, e.g. LLC or C_CORP.

publicId.description: PublicID is the company's shareable public identifier.

IncorporationCountry is the ISO country the entity is incorporated in.
Optional; omitted, null or empty clears it. Any JSON scalar is accepted
and stored as its text.

name.description:
Name is the company's legal name. Required, and it must be a non-empty
string — anything else is refused with the cap table's own validation
error.

additionalTerms.description: AdditionalTerms is free text for anything the fields above do not carry. Optional.

boardApprovalDate.description: BoardApprovalDate is when the board approved it, YYYY-MM-DD.

discountRate.description: DiscountRate is the discount to the next round's price, as a percentage. Optional.

interestRate.description: InterestRate is the annual interest the principal accrues, as a percentage. Optional.

stakeholderId.description: StakeholderID is the lender. It must name a stakeholder of THIS company.

status.description: Status is DRAFT, ACTIVE, PENDING, EXPIRED or CANCELLED.

type.description: Type is CCD, OCD or NOTE.

notes.description: Notes is the convertible notes total.

id.description: ID is the created row's id.

success.description: Success is true when the row was written.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the plan was recorded, in unix milliseconds.

DefaultCancellatonBehavior is what happens to cancelled grants, RETIRE or

boardApprovalDate.description: BoardApprovalDate is when the board adopted the plan, YYYY-MM-DD.

DefaultCancellatonBehavior is what happens to cancelled grants: RETIRE, RETURN_TO_POOL, HOLD_AS_CAPITAL_STOCK or DEFINED_PER_PLAN_SECURITY.

The key is spelled `defaultCancellatonBehavior` — one `l` — because that is
the wire, and correcting it here would silently drop the field.

name.description: Name is the plan's name, e.g. "2026 Stock Option Plan".

planEffectiveDate.description: PlanEffectiveDate is when the plan takes effect, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

shareClassId.description: ShareClassID is the class the plan grants from. It must name a class of THIS company.

data.description: Data is every equity plan on the caller org's cap table, newest first.

options.description: Options is the shares under this stakeholder's non-terminal option grants.

ownershipPct.description:
OwnershipPct is fullyDiluted as a percentage of the company's

shares.description: Shares is the shares this stakeholder holds by certificate.

stakeholderId.description: StakeholderID addresses the stakeholder these totals are for.

count.description: Count is how many instruments there are.

capitalContribution.description: CapitalContribution is cash paid for the shares. Optional.

certificateId.description: CertificateID is the certificate number. It must be UNIQUE within the company; reusing one is refused 409.

cliffYears.description: CliffYears is how long before ANY of the grant vests. A whole number; 0 for no cliff.

companyLegends.description:
CompanyLegends are the restrictive legends printed on the certificate.

A LIST, and it must be sent as one: the bundle substitutes an EMPTY list for
anything that is not an array, so a single string would be accepted and
silently discarded — the certificate issued with no legends and nothing
reporting it.

debtCancelled.description: DebtCancelled is debt forgiven as consideration. Optional.

ipContribution.description: IPContribution is intellectual property assigned as consideration, valued in the company's currency. Optional.

issueDate.description: IssueDate is when the shares were issued, YYYY-MM-DD.

otherContributions.description: OtherContributions is any other consideration, valued in the company's currency. Optional.

pricePerShare.description: PricePerShare is what was paid per share. Optional.

quantity.description: Quantity is how many shares to issue. A whole number above 0.

rule144Date.description: Rule144Date is when the Rule 144 holding period starts, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

shareClassId.description: ShareClassID is the class being issued. It must name a class of THIS company.

stakeholderId.description: StakeholderID is who receives the shares. It must name a stakeholder of THIS company.

status.description: Status is ACTIVE, DRAFT, SIGNED or PENDING.

vestingStartDate.description: VestingStartDate is when vesting begins, YYYY-MM-DD. Optional; defaults to the issue date.

vestingYears.description: VestingYears is the total vesting period. A whole number; 0 for fully vested at issue.

certificateId.description:
CertificateID names the NEW certificate a partial transfer issues, and is
required for one — a partial transfer without it is refused 400. It is unused
by a full transfer, which reassigns the existing certificate.

It must be unique within the company; reusing one is refused 409. Declaring
it is not optional in the way the tag suggests: omitting this field from the
Go type would leave `quantity` accepted and every PARTIAL transfer answering
"certificateId is required" with no way for a caller to supply it — the
silent-drop failure this whole conversion was blocked on, one field wide.

quantity.description:
Quantity is how many shares to move. OPTIONAL, and its absence is not zero:
omitted or null transfers the WHOLE certificate. A value outside 1..held is
refused, so a partial transfer can never over-issue.

A full transfer REASSIGNS the certificate and mints no new one; a partial
transfer splits it and answers with the new share's id. That is the fact a
caller needs from the answer, not from this comment.

shareId.description:
ShareID is the certificate being transferred. Required, and it must name a
share in the caller org's own company — a share id from another tenant
resolves to not-found rather than to another company's certificate.

toStakeholderId.description:
ToStakeholderID is who receives them. Required, and it must reference a
stakeholder of the SAME company; one that does not is refused 400 rather
than creating a dangling holder.

data.description: Data is every issued share certificate, newest first.

city.description: City is the stakeholder's city, if recorded.

companyName.description: CompanyName is the name of the company whose cap table this is.

country.description: Country is the stakeholder's two-letter country code.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the stakeholder was added, in unix milliseconds.

currentRelationship.description:
CurrentRelationship is how the stakeholder relates to the company, e.g.
FOUNDER, INVESTOR or EMPLOYEE.

email.description: Email is the stakeholder's email, unique within the company.

institutionName.description: InstitutionName names the institution, when the stakeholder is one.

name.description: Name is the stakeholder's full name.

state.description: State is the stakeholder's state or province, if recorded.

streetAddress.description: StreetAddress is the stakeholder's street address, if recorded.

taxId.description: TaxID is the stakeholder's tax identifier, if recorded.

zipcode.description: Zipcode is the stakeholder's postal code, if recorded.

currentRelationship.description:
CurrentRelationship is how the stakeholder relates to the company, e.g.
FOUNDER, INVESTOR or EMPLOYEE. This route stores it as sent — unlike
adding a stakeholder, it is not checked against the vocabulary.

email.description:
Email is the stakeholder's email. This route stores it as sent — unlike
adding a stakeholder, it is not checked for shape or uniqueness.

id.description:
ID is the stakeholder to update. It is the path segment: the URL is the
addressing authority, and the org it is resolved in comes from the
caller's principal, so an id from another tenant is simply not found.

institutionName.description: InstitutionName names the institution, when the stakeholder is one.

name.description: Name is the stakeholder's full name.

stakeholderType.description:
StakeholderType is INDIVIDUAL or INSTITUTION. This route stores it as
sent — unlike adding a stakeholder, it is not checked against the
vocabulary.

state.description: State is the stakeholder's state or province.

streetAddress.description: StreetAddress is the stakeholder's street address.

taxId.description: TaxID is the stakeholder's tax identifier.

zipcode.description: Zipcode is the stakeholder's postal code.

byShareClass.description:
ByShareClass is each share class's authorized-versus-issued position, in
class creation order.

byStakeholder.description: ByStakeholder is each stakeholder's position, largest holding first.

company.description: Company names the company the cap table is computed for.

convertibles.description: Convertibles is the capital on SAFEs and notes that have not converted.

totals.description: Totals is the company-wide share count.

id.description: ID is the company id, which is the tenant's own org id.

name.description: Name is the company's legal name.

grantedOptions.description:
GrantedOptions is the shares under non-terminal option grants — grants that
are EXERCISED, EXPIRED or CANCELLED are excluded, so nothing double-counts.

outstandingShares.description: OutstandingShares is the sum of every issued share certificate.

shareClasses.description: ShareClasses is how many share classes the company has authorized.

stakeholders.description: Stakeholders is how many stakeholders the company has.

message.description: Message is the human sentence the cap table wrote, e.g. "Share transferred".

newShareId.description:
NewShareID names the certificate a PARTIAL transfer created. It is null on a
full transfer, which reassigns the existing certificate instead of splitting
it — so null here means "no new certificate", never "the transfer failed".

success.description: Success is true when the transfer was applied.

transferred.description: Transferred is how many shares moved.

message.description: Message is the human sentence the cap table wrote, e.g. "Company updated".

success.description: Success is true when the update was applied.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
